title: Chilled Somen with Dipping Sauce
summary: Delicate chilled Japanese somen noodles served over ice with a cold savoury dipping sauce and fresh aromatics, perfect for a hot day.

steps.title: Soak the kelp
steps.text: Soak the kombu in the 600ml of water for 15 minutes to begin drawing out its flavour. This gentle soak is the base of the dipping sauce's savoury depth.

steps.title: Simmer and remove kelp
steps.text: Bring the water slowly to a bare simmer and lift the kombu out just before it reaches a boil. Boiling kelp turns the stock slimy and bitter, so timing its removal carefully keeps the base clean-tasting.

steps.title: Steep the bonito
steps.text: Add the bonito flakes to the hot liquid, turn off the heat and let them steep for 3 minutes, then strain without pressing on the flakes. Pressing would push cloudy, bitter particles through into the stock, so a gentle strain keeps it clear.

steps.title: Season and chill the sauce
steps.text: Stir the soy sauce and sugar into the strained stock until dissolved, then cool and chill for at least 1 hour. Chilling thoroughly matters here, since the sauce is served cold and needs time to come fully down in temperature for the best flavour.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil, add the somen and stir to separate the strands, cooking for 1-2 minutes until just tender with a firm centre. Somen are very thin and cook fast, so watching them closely stops them turning soft and sticky.

steps.title: Rinse and chill the noodles
steps.text: Drain the noodles and rinse under cold running water, rubbing them gently between your hands to remove surface starch, then plunge them into the iced water. This rinse is essential, since leftover starch is what makes cooked noodles clump together into a sticky mass.

steps.title: Serve with the dip
steps.text: Arrange the chilled noodles in small mounds on ice and set out the cold dipping sauce in individual bowls alongside the spring onions, ginger, sesame seeds and shiso. Dip just a few strands at a time into the sauce as you eat, so the delicate noodles don't become waterlogged.

tips: Rub the noodles gently under cold running water after boiling — skipping this step leaves them sticky and clumped rather than silky and separate.
Pull the kombu out before the stock boils; letting it boil turns the dipping sauce slimy instead of clean and savoury.
Chill the dipping sauce for the full hour if you can — a lukewarm sauce dulls the delicate flavour of the noodles.
Dip small portions of noodles rather than drowning the whole bowl in sauce, which is how the dish is traditionally eaten and keeps the balance of flavours right.
storage: The dipping sauce can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept covered in the fridge. Cooked, rinsed somen are best eaten the same day, as they lose their delicate texture on standing; they aren't suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
